title: Sarcomere Structure Adventure
welcome_lead: Today you'll dissect a sarcomere — the contractile unit of skeletal muscle.
meta_desc: A-Level Biology Muscle Contraction — sarcomere bands (Z, A, I, H), actin and myosin filaments, and slow vs fast twitch fibres.
final_note: You learned the structure of the sarcomere with Z lines, A band, I band and H zone, and the arrangement of thin actin and thick myosin filaments.

walkthroughs.body_html:
A skeletal muscle is bundles of muscle fibres (multinucleate cells).

Inside each fibre are myofibrils — long cylinders made of repeating sarcomeres.

Sarcomeres line up — under a microscope, this gives muscle its striped (striated) appearance.

The sarcomere runs from one Z line to the next.

Bands and zones:
- A band — full length of thick myosin filaments (dark)
- I band — only thin actin between two sarcomeres (light)
- H zone — middle of A band: only thick myosin, no overlap

During contraction: I band and H zone shrink; A band stays the same length.

Two main fibre types tuned for different jobs:

Slow twitch (Type I) — many mitochondria, lots of myoglobin, rich blood supply. Aerobic, fatigue-resistant. Marathon, posture.

Fast twitch (Type II) — fewer mitochondria, lots of glycogen, more phosphocreatine. Anaerobic, powerful but fatigue quickly. Sprinting, jumping.

Most muscles have a mix; the ratio is partly genetic and partly trained.

mcqs.q: What makes the antigen-binding site of an antibody specific to one antigen?
options: Antibodies bind to any antigen they meet first.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
The variable region — its amino acid sequence (and thus shape) differs between antibodies, complementing a specific antigen.
All antibodies have the same binding site; specificity comes from where they go in the body.

mcqs.q: Where do plants get most of their biomass from?
options: Plants get most of their mass from the soil through their roots.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
From carbon dioxide in the air — the carbon in plant tissue comes mostly from CO2 fixed during photosynthesis.

mcqs.q: What is produced in anaerobic respiration in human muscle cells?
options: Anaerobic respiration produces oxygen as a waste product.
Anaerobic respiration produces ethanol and CO2 in humans.
Antibodies bind to any antigen they meet first.
Lactic acid (lactate) and a small amount of ATP — no CO2 or water in this pathway.
